Hi Laura,

Thanks for taking this on. We’re ready to kick off the IdP integration for our Private Control Plane (VPC) deployment. High level asks from Acme:

- Clear break-glass operator account pattern and audit log retention expectations.

Could you share your recommended sync window, how group->role mapping is handled (regexes/attribute mappings), and if Redwood supports SCIM delta only syncs to reduce churn? Jenna and I will coordinate with our security/compliance team.

Hi Samir / Jenna,

Great — happy to run this. Quick answers up front:
- Recommended initial sync window: 02:00–04:00 UTC (low activity for most of your region). We can do a one-time full import and then delta SCIM syncs every 5 minutes for provisioning/changes.
- Group->role mapping: Redwood supports attribute-based mappings (e.g., groups, memberOf) and regex transforms. We generally recommend mapping at the group alias level to avoid changes if your AD DNs change.
- Operator accounts / break-glass: we support a tiered operator role with mandatory 2FA + JIT console elevation for emergency use; we will produce a runbook you can review.

I’ve looped in Rishi to confirm implementation constraints (especially SAML assertion size and if we need to chunk group claims). Also putting Tessa on for production rollout coordination.

Next steps: Rishi will list any SAML/SCIM attribute limits and we'll propose a concrete mapping example based on your metadata. Can you confirm which attribute you expect to use for groups (e.g., memberOf vs groups)?

Hi all,

Technical notes from the runtime side (short list):
1) SAML: Our control plane expects either the standard groups claim or a custom attribute carrying group names; if you send a large memberOf DN list we recommend switching to a groups claim to keep assertion size < 8KB. If you must send big DNs we can accept chunked assertions but it adds complexity.
2) SCIM: We support SCIM v2 with delta support (PATCH + 304 semantics). For initial bootstrap we prefer a full GET /Users and POST/PUT pattern; after that we use incremental syncs every 5 minutes (we store lastSequence/ETag).
3) Service accounts: we create hashed service principal entries; they are not SCIM-provisioned users unless you want them represented in your directory. If you do, we accept a custom 'servicePrincipal' attribute to distinguish them.
4) Role mapping syntax: We support exact group names, prefix match (prefix:DevOps-*), and regex capture groups. Example mapping file (we will provide a template) takes the form: GROUP -> REDWOOD_ROLE (e.g., "acme-private-admins" -> "priv_admin").
5) Audit: Audit logs for SSO/SCIM events are retained 365 days by default for Dedicated/Private customers; we can extend per contract.

Open questions for Acme:
- Which attribute will you source groups from (memberOf vs groups)?
- Do you require provisioning of service accounts in SCIM?
- Any IP allowlist on your side we should know about for the SCIM calls?

I’m attaching the SCIM schema we use and a short checklist for the bootstrap. Priyom will own the operator runbook content.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra

All —

I’ve drafted an operator-access runbook and a sample mapping map for your team to review. Key items included:
- Step-by-step bootstrap: temporary operator accounts -> scoped service accounts -> SCIM delta cutover.
- JIT elevation flow for break-glass (requires IdP-approved MFA assertion, logs an audit event and issues a short-lived token).
- Failback: if SCIM delta fails for >3 cycles we automatically trigger an email + webhook to your SRE with diff output; we keep the previous stable mapping active.
- Timeouts & throttles: SCIM endpoints have 2000 req/min soft throttle for dev/test and a higher burst for Dedicated customers.

Please review the attached runbook and mapping example. I’ve left comments around three spots where we need your group attribute name and whether service accounts should be represented as true users.

Next call proposal: 2028-06-18 14:00 UTC for a 45-minute technical run-through and test account creation.

Thanks,
Priyom Das

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. Jenna and I reviewed the SCIM schema and the runbook; a few quick confirmations from our side:
- We will use groups claim (short list of friendly names) rather than memberOf DNs.
- We do not want service accounts represented as human users in SCIM; instead we will send a servicePrincipal tag in your provisioning object.
- IP allowlist: inbound SCIM requests will originate from a Redwood-managed EIP range; we’ll get you the CIDR block before the run.

We’re good to proceed with the proposed initial full sync on 2028-06-20 02:00–04:00 UTC pending the test account creation. Confirmed for the 2028-06-18 14:00 UTC run-through.

Appreciate the help — looking forward to the run-through.
